keycloak.strategy: IAuthAdapter interface injected via DI token AUTH_ADAPTER_TOKEN. MockAuthAdapter issues real JWTs (jsonwebtoken) signed with JWT_SECRET, stores user credentials in PostgreSQL (bcrypt-hashed passwords), and validates tokens locally. In E11, KeyCloakAuthAdapter replaces MockAuthAdapter with no guard or decorator changes.
keycloak.jwt_payload_shape: { sub: string, email: string, realm_access: { roles: [UserRole] }, iss: string, aud: string, exp: number, iat: number }

stripe.notes: Stripe not applicable to E1 (payment is E4). No Stripe mock needed in E1.

All enums defined in Prisma schema and mirrored in shared-types package

design_decisions.name: mock-auth-di-pattern
design_decisions.decision: AuthModule provides a DI token AUTH_ADAPTER_TOKEN mapped to MockAuthAdapter in E1. In E11, this single token binding is changed to KeyCloakAuthAdapter — zero other code changes.
design_decisions.rationale: Architecture.yaml mock_first_services mandates this pattern. Avoids KeyCloak dependency for E1–E10.

implementation.mock_adapter_internals: MockAuthAdapter stores state in three in-memory Maps: (1) refreshTokens: Map<userId, refreshToken> — invalidated on logout (2) emailVerificationTokens: Map<token, userId> — token = UUID, 24h TTL (3) passwordResetTokens: Map<token, {userId, expiresAt}> — token = UUID, 60min TTL User credentials (email, passwordHash) stored in PostgreSQL User table. JWTs signed with JWT_SECRET env var, 15min access token, 7d refresh token.

design_decisions.e11_swap_path: Replace { provide: AUTH_ADAPTER_TOKEN, useClass: MockAuthAdapter } with { useClass: KeyCloakAuthAdapter } in auth.module.ts. KeyCloakAuthAdapter uses KeyCloak Admin REST API for all operations.

design_decisions.name: repository-pattern
design_decisions.decision: Each NestJS module has a dedicated repository class (UserRepository, AdminRepository)  that owns all Prisma queries for that domain. Services inject repositories; controllers  inject services. PrismaService is injected into repositories.
design_decisions.rationale: quality-standards.yaml design_patterns: 'Repository pattern via Prisma service injection — no direct PrismaClient in controllers or resolvers.'

implementation.rule: No Prisma calls in controllers (AuthController, UserController, AdminController) and no Prisma calls in service methods — all data access via repository methods
implementation.cross_module_data_access: AdminModule uses AdminRepository for all its queries. When AdminModule needs user data, it injects UserService (exported by UserModule) — not UserRepository directly.

design_decisions.name: service-layer-ownership
design_decisions.decision: Controllers handle HTTP binding only (extract DTO, call service, return result). All business logic, validation (beyond DTO structure), authorization checks, and side effects (AuditLog writes) live in the service layer.
design_decisions.rationale: quality-standards.yaml conventions: 'Service layer owns all business logic — controllers handle HTTP binding only.'

implementation.controller_responsibility: Parse DTO from request, call service method, return serialized result via class-transformer. No if/else business logic.
implementation.service_responsibility: Domain invariant enforcement, AuditLog writes, completeness calculation, status transition validation, cross-entity consistency checks.

design_decisions.name: dto-validation-strategy
design_decisions.decision: Global ValidationPipe with whitelist: true and forbidNonWhitelisted: true applied in main.ts. All controller inputs use class-validator decorated DTOs. DTO instances are created via class-transformer plainToInstance before service calls.
design_decisions.rationale: quality-standards.yaml: 'DTOs required for all API request and response shapes (class-validator decorators mandatory for request DTOs).'

design_decisions.name: error-handling-strategy
design_decisions.decision: Global HttpExceptionFilter catches all NestJS HttpExceptions and formats them as { statusCode, message, error, timestamp }. Domain errors are mapped to specific HTTP exceptions in the service layer. Unhandled errors are caught as 500s. Prisma constraint errors (P2002, P2025) are mapped to 409 Conflict and 404 Not Found.
design_decisions.rationale: quality-standards.yaml: 'Error handling complete — no unhandled promise rejections, all Prisma calls in try/catch or wrapped in NestJS HttpException filters.'

design_decisions.name: rbac-guard-pattern
design_decisions.decision: Two guards always applied together on protected routes: (1) JwtAuthGuard — validates JWT Bearer token, populates request.user (2) RolesGuard — reads @Roles() metadata, checks request.user.realm_access.roles Public routes use @Public() decorator that skips JwtAuthGuard.
design_decisions.rationale: Features INV-02 (single role), B1.7.1 (admin-only), B1.7.2 (mentor data), B1.7.4 (unauthenticated)

implementation.jwt_payload_shape: request.user is populated with JwtPayload: { sub (userId), email, realm_access: { roles: [UserRole] }, iss, aud, exp, iat }. RolesGuard reads realm_access.roles[0] for role check. This shape matches KeyCloak's token format exactly — no changes needed in E11.

design_decisions.name: mentor-credential-delivery-on-approval
design_decisions.decision: When admin approves a mentor, AdminService generates a temporary random password, hashes it via MockAuthAdapter, updates User.status to ACTIVE and User.passwordHash. The plain-text temporary password is returned once in the API response for the approving admin to relay manually. It is never logged. An AuditLog entry records the approval event (no password in metadata). In E7, credential delivery will be replaced with SendGrid email — API response will no longer include the temporary password.
design_decisions.rationale: Email delivery (SendGrid/CommsModule) is E7 scope. E1 needs a working credential delivery mechanism.

implementation.e7_migration_note: In E7, remove temporaryCredentials from response and fire SendGrid email via CommsModule instead.

design_decisions.name: token-storage-frontend
design_decisions.decision: Access token stored in localStorage (key: 'felly_access_token'). Refresh token stored in localStorage (key: 'felly_refresh_token'). Axios interceptor reads access token from localStorage and adds Bearer header. On 401 response, interceptor calls POST /auth/refresh and retries original request. Tokens cleared on logout.
design_decisions.rationale: E1 uses a simple localStorage approach for token storage. This is acceptable for the mock auth phase (E1–E10) and for the admin portal. A future security enhancement (E11 or post-launch) can migrate to httpOnly cookies. Architecture.yaml specifies 'JWT Bearer token in Authorization header' — localStorage to header is the simplest implementation.

backend.description: Each domain module (auth, user, admin) has a dedicated *Repository class that owns all Prisma queries for that domain. Services inject the repository and never call PrismaService directly. Repository methods are named after the operation they perform (findById, listPending, updateStatus) — not after SQL operations.
backend.anti_pattern: No Prisma calls in controllers. No cross-module Prisma access (AdminModule does not import UserRepository; it calls UserService methods).

backend.description: Service classes own all business logic: invariant enforcement, state machine transitions, completeness calculation, AuditLog writes, and cross-entity consistency. Controllers are thin HTTP adapters — they extract DTOs, call one service method, and return the result via plainToInstance serialization.

Request DTOs use class-validator decorators. Global ValidationPipe (whitelist, transform). Response DTOs use class-transformer @Exclude()/@Expose() to control serialization. @ApiProperty decorators on all DTO fields for OpenAPI spec generation. plainToInstance(ResponseDto, entity, { excludeExtraneousValues: true }) on all controller returns.

HttpExceptionFilter registered globally in main.ts catches all HttpExceptions. Prisma constraint errors (P2002, P2025) mapped to ConflictException and NotFoundException in service methods. All errors return { statusCode, message, error, timestamp } shape.

JwtAuthGuard and RolesGuard always applied as a pair. @Roles() decorator sets required roles on handler metadata. @CurrentUser() decorator extracts JwtPayload from request. @Public() decorator marks routes that skip JWT validation. This pattern is KeyCloak-compatible — same guards and decorators work when MockAuthAdapter is swapped for KeyCloakAuthAdapter in E11.

Each module's @Module({ exports: [...] }) declares only what other modules may use. No module imports another module's internal service unless it is exported. PrismaModule is @Global() and exports PrismaService (exception to avoid repeated imports). AuthModule exports guards and decorators only — not AuthService.
backend.reference: knowledge/architecture/patterns/modular-monolith.md — 'Module rules: only import via index.ts public API'

backend.scope: All service operations writing to multiple tables
backend.description: Any service method that writes to multiple Prisma models within one logical operation uses this.prisma.$transaction([...]) or the interactive transactions API. Examples: createMentorWithUser() (creates User + MentorProfile atomically), approveMentor() (updates MentorProfile + User status + AuditLog atomically).
backend.reference: quality-standards.yaml: 'Prisma transactions (@prisma/client.$transaction) required for all writes spanning multiple tables'

frontend.description: (auth) route group: unauthenticated pages with auth layout (no nav). (app) / (portal) route group: authenticated pages with full nav layout. Route group name is NOT part of the URL path — (auth)/login renders at /login. Each group has its own layout.tsx defining the shared UI wrapper.
frontend.middleware_guard: middleware.ts runs on all routes to enforce auth — redirects /app/* to /login if no valid token

frontend.pattern: Server Components by Default, 'use client' Where Needed
frontend.description: Page components (page.tsx) are server components unless they need interactivity. Form components, hooks, and anything using useState/useEffect are 'use client'. The QueryProvider wrapper is 'use client' wrapping server layouts. This minimises client bundle size and maximises SSR for public pages.

All API data fetching uses TanStack Query hooks (useQuery for reads, useMutation for writes). Hook files in src/hooks/ encapsulate query keys, fetcher functions, and mutation callbacks. No direct axios calls in page/component files. On successful mutations (profile update, approve/reject), invalidate relevant query keys.

Forms use react-hook-form with useForm<z.infer<typeof schema>>() and zodResolver. Zod schemas defined alongside form components — field-level validation messages match the API's validation error messages. Form submission calls TanStack Query useMutation — no direct axios in form onSubmit handlers.

Single Axios instance configured with base URL from NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL. Request interceptor adds Bearer token from localStorage. Response interceptor handles 401: calls POST /auth/refresh, updates tokens, retries original request once. If refresh fails: clears tokens, redirects to /login.

Components installed via shadcn CLI (npx shadcn add button input card dialog, etc.) into src/components/ui/. These are source files — edit directly if customization needed. cn() utility function (clsx + tailwind-merge) used for conditional classes. All form inputs use shadcn Input and Label for consistent styling and accessibility.

docker_compose.description: Local development services — PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 7 only. KeyCloak excluded (mock auth in E1). OpenSearch excluded (marketplace search is E2).
docker_compose.content:
version: '3.9'
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: felly-postgres
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: felly_club_dev
      POSTGRES_USER: felly
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: fellydev
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U felly -d felly_club_dev"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: felly-redis
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    command: redis-server --save 60 1 --loglevel warning
    volumes:
      - redis_data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

volumes:
  postgres_data:
  redis_data:
